requirement: Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents reviewing code against requirements to inspect every end-user-observable result and branch, including errors and input handling, and verify both that the code fulfills each applicable requirement and that it introduces no additional end-user-observable behavior without an agreed requirement. They MUST explain the requirement and example review criteria in {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`, including test adequacy and justified absence of tests for requirements, and the three outcomes and documented-gap convention in {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Agents MUST mark the roots of a requirement's implementation with `{impl}` and the tests that verify it with `{test}`, leaving code reached from those items unmarked, and use `{cite}` only for related code that does neither, under {cite}`requirements.references.procedure`. When Habeas warns that an item has no recent coverage under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`, they MUST choose its references by that procedure, and for an item no other code reaches, determine whether it is dead code before changing anything. Where requirements interact, agents MUST mark every requirement implemented at the relevant point and explain how their texts jointly account for the behavior. A citation alone MUST NOT count as that explanation.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.cli.behavior_review_guidance`. The requirement obliges the bundled skills to carry guidance text, so the tests assert that text. They do so with `assert_phrases`, `assert_text` and `assert_text_in_order`. These helpers panic when a phrase is missing from the collapsed skill text or from the named `section(...)`. The assertions therefore enforce the guidance.

Obligation-to-test mapping, all in `tests/authoring_cli.rs`:

- **Inspect every observable result and branch, and add no unagreed behavior.** `fn[bundled_skills_direct_behavior_review_against_requirements]` asserts the following.
  - `habeas-requirements` says "Every end-user-observable result of the code, including errors and input handling, must follow from a requirement the user agreed to".
  - `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` says "distinct observable branches" and "every observable branch has been reviewed".
  - `habeas-evidence` says "Behavior with no requirement needs one agreed with the user".
  - The "What the review checks" section says "The supervising agent must still check that the code fulfills each applicable requirement".
- **Explain `requirements.ci.review_criteria`.** The same test asserts the "What the review checks" section of `habeas-requirements` contains these points:
  - assertions that contradict the requirement;
  - the marking gap for a standalone test without `{test}`;
  - untested obligations, boundaries and failure cases;
  - the narrow test-omission exemption, and that "unchanged, distinct, or present" always needs a test;
  - how an example's review is judged;
  - that one acknowledged gap does not excuse others.

  It also asserts that `habeas-evidence` points to that section for a false rationale.
- **Explain `requirements.ci.outcomes`.** The test asserts the three outcomes (`true`, `false`, FIXME) in `habeas-evidence`. It also asserts the FIXME convention: the example `{"FIXME": [...]}`, the `// :github:` option line, and "A plain `FIXME` or `TODO` comment does not count". For deferring a gap, it asserts "To defer a requirement gap the user agrees to, use `{fixme}`" in `habeas-requirements`.
- **`{test}` on tests, `{impl}` on roots, unmarked reached code, and `{cite}` only for related code.** The following tests assert this.
  - The "Choosing references" assertions in `fn[bundled_skills_direct_behavior_review_against_requirements]` cover the `{test}`, `{impl}` and `{cite}` rules.
  - `fn[bundled_skills_mark_roots_and_handle_uncovered_items]` asserts the definition of a root and that "Helpers the test calls need nothing". It also asserts "Leave what it reaches unmarked" and "Callers don't count". It further asserts that the other skills do not restate the root definition.
  - `fn[bundled_skills_direct_the_reference_procedure_and_report_items_without_one]` asserts the ordered procedure steps in order and that the other skills refer to it instead of restating it.
- **Coverage warnings: follow the procedure, and check for dead code before changing an unreached item.** `fn[bundled_skills_mark_roots_and_handle_uncovered_items]` asserts the "Uncovered Rust items" section of `habeas-evidence` in order. That section says to choose references by "Choosing references". It says to determine "whether it is a requirement root, an entry point, an item that serves other code, or dead code" before changing, and to report dead code without editing it. It also has the decision table. The same test asserts that references come from a reference or a current read, and not from a search.
- **Interacting requirements.** `fn[bundled_skills_direct_behavior_review_against_requirements]` asserts that `habeas-requirements` says to mark each requirement with `{impl}` where it applies and add fenced commentary on how they combine. It asserts that "a reference alone would not say why `^C` is accepted". It also asserts the matching `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` sentence.

No obligation lacks a test. The tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, and the helpers they reach need none. The tests check a representative set of phrases rather than every criterion in `requirements.ci.review_criteria` word for word, such as state transitions. The subject asks only that the skills explain those criteria, "including test adequacy and justified absence of tests". Both of those are asserted. I found no plausible violation of the stated obligations that these assertions would accept. There are no `{fixme}` acknowledgments and none are needed.

text: :::{req} behavior_review_guidance

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents reviewing code against requirements to inspect every end-user-observable result and branch, including errors and input handling, and verify both that the code fulfills each applicable requirement and that it introduces no additional end-user-observable behavior without an agreed requirement. They MUST explain the requirement and example review criteria in {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`, including test adequacy and justified absence of tests for requirements, and the three outcomes and documented-gap convention in {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Agents MUST mark the roots of a requirement's implementation with `{impl}` and the tests that verify it with `{test}`, leaving code reached from those items unmarked, and use `{cite}` only for related code that does neither, under {cite}`requirements.references.procedure`. When Habeas warns that an item has no recent coverage under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`, they MUST choose its references by that procedure, and for an item no other code reaches, determine whether it is dead code before changing anything. Where requirements interact, agents MUST mark every requirement implemented at the relevant point and explain how their texts jointly account for the behavior. A citation alone MUST NOT count as that explanation.
:::{req} review_criteria
The reviewer MUST assess the named subject using its text, referenced requirements,
and terminology definitions. For a requirement, the reviewer MUST assess whether
the reviewed tests adequately check its stated obligations, including relevant
input classes, boundaries, condition combinations, state transitions, and failure
cases. These cases MUST follow from the requirement's obligations; the reviewer
MUST NOT require behavior for inputs the text leaves unspecified. The reviewer
MUST derive expected outcomes from the text, inspect the tests and relevant
helpers or fixtures, and map each obligation assessed here to concrete test
inputs and assertions in the rationale. It MUST separately identify obligations
delegated to a refining requirement or a distributed site's review and any
established testing exemptions. It MUST assess both whether expected results conform
to the text and whether the assertions enforce those results.
For every proposed adequacy gap, the reviewer MUST describe plausible behavior
that violates a stated obligation but would be accepted by the reviewed tests,
and explain which missing scenarios or weak assertions allow it. For an incorrect
expected result, it MUST instead identify the assertion and explain its conflict
with the text. A counterexample MUST identify a requirement-relevant distinction
that the tests miss; another untested value in an already represented input class
MUST NOT by itself establish a gap without explaining why it could expose
different required behavior. It MUST check other relevant tests and helpers before reporting a
gap and distinguish missing information from an established inadequacy. A marking
gap or an ambiguity MUST be identified as such, without requiring a behavioral
counterexample. A judgment of `true` MUST mean the reviewed tests adequately check
the subject under these criteria, including the testing exemptions of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.testing_bar`; it MUST NOT assert implementation
correctness. The reviewer MAY request implementation source to resolve a
specific question and MUST state that question in its rationale. It MUST NOT
derive expected behavior from the implementation or assess implementation
correctness, implementation reachability, or unspecified implementation behavior
as additional tasks.
When another requirement implements part of the subject, the
reviewer MUST assess whether its text carries out that part, and MUST NOT
reassess its implementation, tests, or evidence; that requirement is assessed
separately. When there are no tests, the reviewer MUST apply the testing
exemptions of {cite}`requirements.authoring.testing_bar` and explain any
exemption it establishes.
The reviewer MUST apply these rules in every assessment. MUST and MUST NOT state
obligations; a SHOULD MUST impose an obligation unless the subject's text or a
source comment gives a reason it does not apply, and the reviewer MUST apply the
testing criteria to every applicable SHOULD in a test-adequacy assessment and
explain each exception in the rationale; MAY imposes nothing to
check; examples and sample output in the text illustrate the obligations its
prose states and bind their exact form only where the text says so. When the subject's

text admits two readings its wording supports equally and they lead to different conclusions, such as whether code conforms or which role a citation calls for, the ambiguity MUST be treated as a gap and the rationale MUST name
the readings. A test that verifies the subject without a `{test}` reference to it
MUST be treated as a marking gap; a helper reached from a marked test MUST NOT
need a reference of its own. A gap MUST be
reported only for a specific obligation with relevant sources the reviewer
has read. Before reporting a missing test, the reviewer MUST perform targeted
discovery of relevant tests and identify the missing scenario; an absent test
MUST NOT require an invented source location. Style, performance, logging, how

helpers are factored, robustness the text does not require, and silently ignoring input the text does not mention MUST NOT be treated as gaps, and the reviewer MUST NOT report bugs or issues outside the
subject's text.
For a distributed requirement under {cite}`requirements.references.distributed`,
the reviewer MUST also assess the requirement and its queries. Each obligation
MUST be either one that each site upholds on its own, checked by its review under
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, or one that particular code carries
out, assessed as above through its `{impl}` and `{test}` references; an
obligation neither covers MUST be treated as a gap. The reviewer MUST judge whether
each query's conditions are adequate and adequately tested: the site queries
MUST select every place the text's description of a site covers and no place
outside the requirement's stated scope, and each query's `match` and `no_match`
snippets MUST test its conditions as tests of code would, judged as such; a
condition without a snippet of its own MUST NOT by itself be treated as a gap. Because queries are heuristics, the reviewer MUST
judge them by a preponderance of the evidence, asking whether it is more likely
than not that the site queries find the places the requirement applies: a
specific place in the sources that a site query misses or wrongly selects MUST be
treated as a gap, and a form that does not occur in the sources MUST NOT.
Obligations that decide which places are sites, such as a naming rule, MUST be
checked by the reviewer's search of the sources. Violation queries direct site
reviews to likely problems; the reviewer SHOULD note constructs they miss, but
their incompleteness MUST NOT by itself make the determination false. Any other
gap in the queries or snippets MUST be treated as a gap under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, even when the code is correct. The reviewer SHOULD run each site query once, scan its matches,
and search briefly for the construct the text describes, and MUST NOT review each
site or treat a site without an `{impl}` reference as a gap.
For an example, the reviewer MUST assess whether tests exist whose setup and
assertions cover its scenario and expected outcomes. The rationale MUST identify
the relevant sources and explain the testing judgment for a
requirement, or the test coverage for an example. Referenced requirements provide
context; they MUST NOT become additional subjects to assess in full.
:::{req} outcomes
Every assessment judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`:
- `true`: the reviewed tests adequately check a requirement or example under
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`, including applicable testing
exemptions and obligations assessed by a refining requirement or a site's
own review. For a citation or site review, the review finds no gap under its
own task.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
and the gaps are not all acknowledged by `{fixme}` references to it.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and `{fixme}` references to
the subject acknowledge every one of those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the
gaps and their source locations in the rationale and record their issue
references or other identifying content from the supplied acknowledgments or
inputs.
The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`{"FIXME": ["example/queue#125", "rust-lang/rust#123"]}`. A gap MUST count as
acknowledged only by a `{fixme}` reference under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` whose body describes that gap and that
references the assessed definition, or, for a site review, the distributed requirement from within that site; a citation review MUST NOT accept a `{fixme}`; a plain
`FIXME` comment, another marker such as `TODO`, or prose MUST NOT. The strings
MUST list each distinct issue reference the acknowledging `{fixme}` references
name in their option lines, as written after `:github:`, and, for a `{fixme}`
naming no issue, its body's words, without comment delimiters, joined by single
spaces. A `{fixme}` reference describing a gap that the review establishes no
longer exists within its task's scope MUST itself be treated as a gap. A reference
describing only an implementation defect MUST NOT create a test-adequacy gap or
require implementation review; it MUST acknowledge a testing gap only when its
body describes that same gap. A `{fixme}` naming a GitHub issue that
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads` reports closed MUST NOT count as
acknowledging its gap. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in recorded evidence
inputs or, for an acknowledgment supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`, the reference-set digest covering
that acknowledgment.
:::{req} procedure
A source item MUST choose its references under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
for each candidate definition by this procedure, and MAY carry several:
1. If the item is a test designed to verify the definition, it MUST use
`{test}`. A test helper a reviewer reaches by following such a test needs no
reference to the definition.
2. Otherwise, if the item is a root of the definition's implementation, it
MUST use `{impl}`. Code or a type carries out part of a definition when it
makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case
the definition specifies, or when the definition constrains its shape:
fields, variants, serialized form, or validation. A root is such an item
that no other item marked `{impl}` for the definition reaches, where an item
reaches what it calls, the types it uses, and the implementations of trait
methods it calls, and what those reach in turn. An item reached from a root
needs no reference to the definition. An item that is a site of a distributed definition
under {cite}`requirements.references.distributed` needs no reference to it;
its site review covers it.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
4. If the item carries no reference after applying steps 1 to 3 to every
definition and no assessment reads it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, it MUST cite the
built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util` when it
serves other code. An item that does neither carries out behavior that needs
a requirement, or is not needed.
A `{fixme}` reference is added independently of this procedure, and MUST NOT
count as an item's reference for {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
:::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST report the number
of nodes without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, except items inside a module
named `tests`, using the following summary:
```text
N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them.
The summary MUST report zero when no nodes have warnings. Default output MUST
NOT list individual coverage warnings or coverage-history details, including
with `status --all` or `status --verbose`.
`habeas status --coverage` MUST list every warning, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, and report incomplete coverage history when applicable.
A warning MUST NOT fail validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read
Git history.
